title: Automated user-data purge pipeline and attestations for RTBF
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Business context: Customers in regulated markets require a fully auditable Right-To-Be-Forgotten (RTBF) workflow that guarantees complete deletion of personal data across hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket scopes a product-first implementation that automates purge requests, verifies deletion across services, attaches cryptographic attestations where feasible, and surfaces evidence in Console and automated reports. Goals: (1) provide a self-service RTBF endpoint and Console flow, (2) automate cross-service purge orchestration including cache, logs, and backups, (3) generate immutable evidence artifacts for compliance reviews, (4) support data-residency scoping and retention policy overrides per customer. This is a cross-functional initiative requiring runtime, infra, console, and legal sign-off.
in_scope: Expose RTBF API and Console flow for admins
Orchestrate purges across model serving KV caches, request logs, metrics samplers, and analytics pipelines
Generate a signed purge attestation (timestamped, SHA256 digest of deleted object IDs) stored in customer audit bucket
Automated purge verification jobs with reconciliation reports
Retention settings UI with per-organization overrides and region-scoped controls
out_of_scope: Automated deletion of third-party partner copies (handled by contract)
Long-term backups of archived cold storage — process will mark items for eventual deletion and flag for manual follow-up
Legal/forensic eDiscovery workflows beyond issuance of attestations
requirements: RTBF API: POST /v1/admin/purge-requests with scope, reason, requester, and residency constraint
Purge orchestration engine that queues tasks and retries across subsystems with idempotency
Verification service that polls target subsystems and produces a final reconciliation report stating success/failure per subsystem
Attach a signed attestation blob to the customer's audit directory (S3/GCS) with a human-readable summary and machine-verifiable digest
Console: admin flow to create/track purge requests, view verification status, download attestation and CSV of deleted object ids
Retention policy editor in Console with default and per-org overrides, and enforcement that interacts with the orchestration engine
non_functional: End-to-end RTBF CPU/worker time per request should be under 5 minutes for small tenants (<= 100k keys) under normal conditions
System must store immutable audit artifacts for minimum 7 years when requested by enterprise plan
Attestations should be signed with a key managed by Redwood KMS; private deployments must support customer KMS integration (guide in runbook)
All operations must be logged with correlation_id for traceability and must not expose PII in logs
acceptance_criteria: API and Console flows exist and can create purge requests with residency constraints
Orchestration engine completes purges across at least three representative subsystems in staging: serving KV cache, request logs index, analytics events store
Signed attestation stored in audited bucket and downloadable via Console
Automated reconciliation report shows pass/fail per subsystem and includes cryptographic digests
E2E tests that simulate RTBF request and validate absence of the test user in targeted subsystems
Security review approved by security@redwood and legal attestation template reviewed by legal@redwood
success_metrics: % of purge requests that complete without manual intervention (target >= 95%)
Mean time to final attestation (target < 30 minutes for <= 1M keys)
Number of compliance incidents related to deletion failures (target 0 post-launch)
Time saved for Solutions/Support when answering deletion inquiries (baseline TBD)
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha - enable for Redwood-managed hosted accounts on staging only; collect telemetry and corner cases
Phase 2: Beta - opt-in for select enterprise tenants with dedicated support; enable signed attestations and retention UI
Phase 3: General availability - enable for all hosted accounts and release Console and API docs; ship runbooks for Dedicated/Private customers
Phase 4: Private/VPC - docs and assisted deployment for customers to use their KMS and audit buckets; optional close collaboration with SRE
dependencies: ENG-2601 (KV cache delete API and streaming invalidation)
ENG-2899 (Console retention settings UI and RBAC)
notes_for_engineering: Key trade-offs: immediate physical deletion vs. logical deletion + timestamped attestation. For performance and safety, implement two-tier purge: logical tombstone + background physical sweep with retry and verification; produce attestation once all subsystems report success. Ensure deletion flows are idempotent and support resume. For Private installs, require explicit KMS integration to sign attestations. Provide a non-PII-scrubbed test harness for E2E testing in staging.
